items.prompt:
What is a keyboard used for?

A) To draw pictures on paper
B) To type letters and words on a screen
items.answer: B) To type letters and words on a screen

steps: A keyboard has keys for letters and numbers that you press to type words onto a computer or tablet screen.

items.prompt:
Which key removes the last letter you typed?

A) Enter
B) Backspace

steps: The backspace key deletes the last character typed. It is useful for fixing mistakes.

items.prompt:
What is one advantage of sharing a story on a class website?

A) Only the teacher can read it.
B) Many people can read it at the same time from anywhere.
items.answer: B) Many people can read it at the same time from anywhere.

steps: Digital publishing allows wide, instant access. Many readers can open the same file simultaneously.

items.prompt: Compare typing to handwriting. Name one advantage of each.
items.answer: Typing advantage: easy to fix mistakes by pressing backspace and can be shared electronically. Handwriting advantage: can be done anywhere without electricity or a device.

steps: Consider: when is each method more practical?
Typing wins for sharing and editing. Handwriting wins for portability.

items.prompt:
A student finishes typing her story. What should she do BEFORE publishing it digitally?

A) Delete the whole thing and start over.
B) Proofread for spelling and punctuation errors and make any final revisions.
items.answer: B) Proofread for spelling and punctuation errors and make any final revisions.

steps: Before publishing, writers always proofread and revise to make sure the writing is polished and correct.

items.prompt:
Two students want to write a story together using a digital tool. Which tool would work best?

A) A shared document on a tablet or computer where both students can type and see changes
B) Two separate pieces of paper
items.answer: A) A shared document on a tablet or computer where both students can type and see changes

steps: A shared document allows both students to type and read each other's work in real time, which is not possible with two separate pieces of paper.

items.prompt: Describe how a class could use digital tools to write and publish a class newspaper. Include at least three steps.
items.answer: Step 1: Each student writes an article about a school topic (drafting). Step 2: Students type their articles on the class computer and make revisions with the teacher's help. Step 3: The teacher combines all articles into one digital document formatted like a newspaper. Step 4: The newspaper is emailed to all families or posted on the school website so everyone can read it.

steps: Draft → type → revise → combine → publish online or by email.
Each step uses a digital tool and moves toward reaching a wider audience.

items.prompt: Explain in your own words why learning to use digital writing tools is an important skill for a first grader. Give TWO reasons.
items.answer: Reason 1: Most schoolwork and jobs in the future will require typing and using computers, so starting early makes students more prepared and confident. Reason 2: Digital tools allow students to share their writing with a much wider audience than handwriting can, which teaches them that writing has real-world purpose and impact.

steps: Think about communication and audience reach.
